text.title: Futures edge up after Treasury selloff; Nvidia CEO exit, Microsoft outage in focus
text.summary: US stock futures are modestly higher after Thursday's declines, when the S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Russell 2000 fell 1.7%. Treasury yields jumped on inflation worries, and Nvidia's CEO departure and a Microsoft outage are driving single-stock headlines. Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 2.8% overnight, with no single clear driver in the headlines.

drivers.t: The 10-year yield rose 10bp to 5.10% and the 2-year rose 13bp to 4.86%. Treasuries are set for their worst week since 'liberation day' after higher-than-expected inflation and hawkish remarks from Fed officials.
Jensen Huang's resignation has put Nvidia's AI financing strategy in focus. The stock has shed nearly $500 billion in market value this week and is still a roughly $4 trillion company.
Microsoft fell in premarket trade as a worldwide outage hit Outlook, Teams and 365, including its Copilot tool. The company says it is seeing 'encouraging recovery signals'.
The Russell 2000 dropped 1.7%, far more than the large-cap indexes, on a day yields climbed. The headlines give no single clear driver for the gap.

Bitcoin is down 3.1% at about $69,154 and fell below $70,000 for the first time since August. It is on track for a sixth straight weekly loss as expectations of higher rates and a risk-off mood weigh.
WTI is little changed at $88.56, down 0.2%. The IEA says the world oil market is returning to surplus as Gulf exports recover.
